papers.title: LEASH: Uncertainty-Aware Weak-to-Strong Escalation and Oversight for Computer-Use Agents
papers.problem: Computer-use agents cost too much when a top model runs every step, and a small model alone often fails.
papers.fix: LEASH calls the strong model only when the small one seems unsure, hitting 73.66% success at 19.2% lower cost.
papers.practicalUseCase: You can match a top model's results for less money, so route easy steps to a small model.
papers.limitation: Results come from one benchmark, OSWorld, with four model families.

papers.title: Diminishing Returns of Data in Sparse Autoencoders: Functional Behavior does not Guarantee Feature Reproducibility
papers.problem: Teams train sparse autoencoders on billions of tokens, but nobody tested whether that much data is needed.
papers.fix: Less data nearly matches full-data quality, but matched features rise only from 2% at 5M tokens to 29% at 50M.
papers.practicalUseCase: You can train cheaper for quick tests, but you must use more data when you want stable, repeatable features.
papers.limitation: The tests cover four architectures and three language models, with a 500M-token reference.

papers.title: Scalable Weak-to-Strong Verifier Hardening for Agent Environments
papers.problem: Cheating agents can trick the code that scores them, which gives false rewards and wrong evaluations.
papers.fix: An automatic hacker-fixer loop inside an isolated sandbox cuts attack success on Terminal Bench, KernelBench, and SETA.
papers.practicalUseCase: If you build agent tests, run an attacker model against your scorer and fix every hole before training.
papers.limitation: Defense gets stronger only as you spend more loop iterations, so the budget limits it.

papers.title: Behavioral Compositionality of Sparse Autoencoder Representations
papers.problem: Nobody knew whether the effects of sparse autoencoder features add up cleanly when you combine them.
papers.fix: Learned features add up better than random ones; pairwise terms lift steering rank fidelity from 0.5874 to 0.7790.
papers.practicalUseCase: Do not trust single-feature explanations or edits alone, because combined features interact and need pairwise checks.
papers.limitation: The tests cover 18 model and behavior settings, so results may differ for other models.

papers.title: Trends and Determinants of Sustainability Sukuk Issuance: Evidence from Global Markets
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Sustainability sukuk grew fast, but nobody had documented what drives how big each issue is.
papers.fix: In 11,944 sukuk issues from 2012 to 2022, better security, longer terms, and USD or Euro currency mean larger issues.
papers.practicalUseCase: Issuers who want bigger sustainability sukuk should use strong security, longer terms, and equity-based contracts, not sale-based ones.
papers.limitation: The data stops at 2022 and shows links between factors and size, not cause.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence and Big Data Strategies to Enhance Islamic Banks’ Competitiveness and Sustainable Development
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Islamic banks in Jordan lacked evidence on whether artificial intelligence and big data help them compete and last.
papers.fix: In surveyed Jordanian banks, AI use, data analysis, and data management all link to higher competitiveness and sustainable development.
papers.practicalUseCase: Bank leaders should invest in AI and data practices, not only staff digital skills, to improve sustainable development.
papers.limitation: The survey covers 214 managers in 15 Jordanian Islamic banks at one point in time.

papers.title: ICT, High-Tech Exports, and Institutions as Drivers of Bank Expansion Growth in a Dual Banking System
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Banks in dual systems had unclear evidence on which factors drive their growth.
papers.fix: In 218 banks across 12 countries from 2010 to 2023, technology adoption is the strongest driver of bank growth.
papers.practicalUseCase: Regulators should fund digital infrastructure and strong governance, because Islamic banks lean on institutional integrity to grow.
papers.limitation: The sample covers 12 countries and 2010 to 2023, so it may not fit other markets.

papers.title: Determinants of Financial Inclusion in the OIC and OECD Countries: Are They Different?
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.institution: International Centre for Education in Islamic Finance
papers.problem: Many Muslim-majority countries still exclude people from financial services, even as Islamic finance expanded.
papers.fix: In 35 countries from 2005 to 2021, income, education, institutions, and internet access drive financial inclusion in OIC countries.
papers.practicalUseCase: OIC governments should invest in digital infrastructure, youth and women empowerment, and income growth.
papers.limitation: The study covers only 35 countries from 2005 to 2021 and shows links, not cause.

papers.title: Sustainability Committees and Environmental Initiatives: Insights from Dual Banking Systems in Emerging Markets
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Banks in dual systems set up sustainability committees, but their effect on real environmental work was unclear.
papers.fix: Committees link to better environmental scores in all banks, but in Islamic banks they affect only overall and resource scores.
papers.practicalUseCase: Islamic bank boards should check that committees produce green products and innovation, not only good scores.
papers.limitation: The panel data shows links in emerging markets, not proof that committees cause the results.

papers.title: Global prevalence of impostor phenomenon in medical students: A systematic review and meta-analysis
papers.institution: National University Toribio Rodríguez de Mendoza
papers.problem: Medical students face constant exams and peer comparison, and nobody had pooled how often they feel like impostors.
papers.fix: Impostor feelings are common among medical students worldwide, though results vary by sampling method and region.
papers.practicalUseCase: If you train or mentor students, expect impostor feelings and teach coping skills early.
papers.limitation: Results varied a lot between studies, so the pooled number is rough.

papers.title: Exploring the influencing factors of academic doctoral students’ academic innovation behavior in the context of generative artificial intelligence: Self-determination theory and motivation-opportunity-ability perspectives
papers.problem: Doctoral students use generative AI heavily, but little was known about what drives their academic innovation.
papers.fix: Inner and outer motivation work together to raise innovation, while unmet basic needs sharply cut it.
papers.practicalUseCase: Supervisors should meet students' basic needs and give research support, because unmotivated students stop exploring.
papers.limitation: The survey uses one-time self-reports from chemistry students, so it cannot prove cause.
